title: Asynchronous Blob conversion bypasses relay generation isolation
test: Scratch browser check watch-check13-run.mjs with watch-check13-page/ (lane `watch` scratchpad, Playwright lock held): Vite 8.3.4 bundles a page that imports `io` from socket.io-client and the app's own createSocketOptions() from src/lib/socketOptions.mjs (so the browser field and exports resolve as in the app build); a real socket.io 4.8.4 server emits 'media-chunk' {generation, chunk: Buffer} exactly as lib/socket.js forwards it (toBinaryChunk always yields a Node Buffer), and the page records the chunk's type in onChunk's terms (instanceof Blob / ArrayBuffer). Run in headless Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, each with the app's options (websocket first, tryAllTransports), websocket only and polling only. Output kept in watch-check13-browser-output.txt.
proof: The claim does not hold as a defect. Its reading of the code is right: src/WatchView.jsx:478 checks `payload.generation !== selectedGeneration` before `data.arrayBuffer().then(enqueueChunk)` (484-486), enqueueChunk (438-474) never re-checks the generation or relayCleanupDone, and onMediaInit (501-506) clears the queue and moves selectedGeneration, so a Blob read still pending across a media-init would push old-generation bytes into the new queue. But that branch never runs: Nextra's viewers never receive a Blob. The client never sets binaryType (src/lib/socketOptions.mjs, src/context/SocketContext.jsx), engine.io-client 6.6.6's browser default is 'arraybuffer' (build/esm/globals.js:21 `defaultBinaryType = "arraybuffer"`, mapped over globals.node.js by its browser field; the shipped dist bundle has `ye=`arraybuffer`` and no 'blob'), websocket.js:29 sets `ws.binaryType = this.socket.binaryType`, and engine.io-parser's decodePacket.browser.js mapBinary returns an ArrayBuffer for 'arraybuffer' on every transport (WebSocket frames, base64 long-polling, WebTransport). The browser check confirms it: 27 of 27 chunks arrived as '[object ArrayBuffer]' (isBlob false, engine binaryType 'arraybuffer') in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit over websocket and polling, with the app's options too ('rows=27 blobRows=0 errors=0'). With an ArrayBuffer, onChunk takes the synchronous branch (490-491) and enqueueChunk runs in the same task as the generation check, so no media-init can come between them, and nothing is left running for cleanup to cancel. Original code: `git diff ac1c688 HEAD -- src/WatchView.jsx` is empty (the quoted lines are the same), the client at ac1c688 also set no binaryType, and package.json/package-lock.json are unchanged (socket.io-client 4.8.4, engine.io-client 6.6.6), so it was not real there either. No file changed.
